context.coverage_summary: 9 acceptance criteria (AC1-AC9) from handoffs/WF02-REQ186-20260829/step-03-test-designer.json, each mapped to >=1 test case in test/specs/REQ-186.md. AC1 (tenant-scoped table + partial index) verified via information_schema/pg_indexes inspection. AC2/AC3 (status and recurrence CHECK constraints) verified via raw SQL inserts bypassing the changeset layer, asserting Postgrex check_violation. AC4 (past vs future fire_at) has two explicit tests. AC5 (double-poll idempotency) verified via two poll_and_fire/1 calls. AC6 (failing fire attempt continues the cycle) has two tests: an integration-level test using a timer with no active instance_projections row (a natural, organic {:error, :instance_not_started} failure from EventStore.append/2's own active_instance_guard, exercised alongside a second, real-firing timer to prove the cycle continues), plus a narrower unit test calling Scheduler.attempt_fire/2 with a syntactically invalid UUID to force a genuine Ecto.Query.CastError raise and prove the outer try/rescue never lets it escape. AC7 (max-retries exhaustion) drives a timer through 2 overridden max_fire_retries failures, asserting failed status, failed_at, exactly one dlq_entries row, and no further reattempt. AC8 (config defaults + override) has three tests in scheduler_test.exs (defaults, override, max_timers_per_cycle actually bounding claim_due_timer_ids/2) plus one Poller-specific test in poller_test.exs starting a real Poller GenServer and proving the overridden poll_interval_ms -- not the 5000ms default -- governs a real second tick. AC9 (no route/controller) is a structural file-content check with no git-history dependency (this project's own documented anti-pattern against hardcoded commit SHAs, per test/letflow/dlq_test.exs's own AC6 comment).
context.mutation_testing_summary: 6 mutations applied one at a time to lib/letflow/scheduler.ex / lib/letflow/scheduler/poller.ex, each reverted via git checkout before the next: (1) removed the FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED lock in claim_due_timer_ids/2 -- NOT caught (18/18 still passed); no acceptance criterion in this requirement's scope exercises concurrent claimers, so no test asserts on row-locking behavior -- flagged, not silently hidden. (2) hardcoded fired_late to false in do_fire/2 -- caught (17/18, AC4 test failed). (3) flipped the max-retries comparison from >= to > in record_fire_failure/2 -- caught (17/18, AC7 test failed). (4) hardcoded the DLQ-landing enqueue call's prefix to "public" instead of tenant_schema -- caught (17/18, AC7 test failed, no dlq_entries row found in the tenant schema). (5) removed the fire_error_count + 1 increment (new_count = timer.fire_error_count instead of + 1) -- caught (16/18, both AC6 and AC7 tests failed). (6) hardcoded the Poller's schedule_next_tick/0 delay to 5_000 instead of reading Scheduler.poll_interval_ms/0 -- caught (17/18, the poller_test.exs AC8 test failed). After each mutation, git diff lib/letflow/scheduler.ex lib/letflow/scheduler/poller.ex lib/letflow/scheduler/timer.ex was confirmed empty (byte-identical to the committed state) before the next mutation. 5 of 6 mutations caught; the uncaught one (row-locking removal) is a genuine, disclosed coverage gap outside this requirement's stated acceptance criteria, not a silently-missed one.
context.known_gap: Mutation (1) above (FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED removal) is not caught by any test in this suite -- no acceptance criterion requires testing concurrent claimers racing the same due timer, and DIRECTIVE T-1/this project's test conventions do not call for a multi-process concurrency test here. Recorded for TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's own judgment on whether this gap is acceptable given AC1-AC9's literal scope.
